scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five NIFTY 50 constituents — HCL Technologies, HDFC Life Insurance, Hindalco Industries, Hindustan Unilever, ICICI Bank — from each company's own latest SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) shareholding-pattern filing where that filing could be opened directly (HCL Technologies, HDFC Life, Hindalco: quarter ended 30 June 2026, opened on the companies' own investor-relations sites), plus the mandatory BlackRock/Vanguard/NBIM/GIC/Capital Group/Fidelity/KIA/ADIA/GQG comparison set and LIC of India as the domestic control, tested against every primary filing actually opened. For Hindustan Unilever and ICICI Bank, hul.co.in returned an Akamai 'Access Denied' (403) on every route tried (curl with multiple user agents, WebFetch) and icici.bank.in's investor pages are client-rendered shells with no server-side PDF links reachable in this pass, so those two companies are recorded at screener.in aggregate only (tier reported), with the primary-source attempts recorded as voids. Also recorded: two non-comparison-set foreign FPI holders found named (Artisan International Value Fund in HCL Technologies; Camas Investments Pte. Ltd. in HDFC Life), a foreign-classified promoter-group entity that is the founder family's own holding vehicle rather than third-party foreign capital (HCL Holdings Private Ltd., via the discretionary Vama Sundari Trust), and a GDR depositary bank correctly flagged as a custodian rather than a beneficial owner (Morgan Guaranty Trust Company of New York, for Hindalco's GDRs). Left out: adviser mandates and SEBI/RBI rule-change history (out of this batch's scope), and any holder below the 1% individual-naming threshold, which in three of the five filings is disclosed only as an unbroken category aggregate.

Every date claimed in this file was cross-checked against the 'quarter ended' field printed inside the PDF itself, not inferred from the URL.

symmetryCheck: Run on the same three primary filings (HCL Technologies, HDFC Life, Hindalco), LIC appears as a named ≥1% domestic holder in exactly one of three (Hindalco, 4.59%) — in HCL Technologies and HDFC Life, the domestic 'Insurance Companies' line is disclosed only as an unbroken aggregate (8.32% across 39 holders; 2.20% across 30 holders respectively), with no individual name broken out, so LIC's absence there is a filing-format artefact, not evidence LIC holds nothing. The non-BlackRock comparison holders fared no better than BlackRock/Vanguard at crossing the 1% naming threshold: NBIM crossed it once (HDFC Life, 1.14%), GIC crossed it once (Hindalco, 2.65%), and Capital Group, Fidelity, Kuwait Investment Authority, ADIA and GQG Partners crossed it zero times across all three filings — the same fragmentation-across-many-registered-vehicles pattern documented in the main holders.json file recurs here. The two largest 'foreign' lines found in this batch by far are not portfolio investors at all: HCL Holdings Private Ltd (16.46% of HCL Technologies) is the founder family's own trust-held vehicle, and Morgan Guaranty Trust Company of New York (4.18% of Hindalco) is a GDR custodian bank holding shares on behalf of unnamed GDR holders. Read naively, a filing's raw 'Institutions (Foreign)' or Table II 'Foreign' aggregate therefore overstates genuine third-party foreign portfolio ownership by conflating family trusts and custodian balancing figures with actual outside investors — the same distortion the BAT/Suzuki promoter stakes illustrated in the main holders.json file, now shown to recur even inside the 'Foreign' promoter and depositary lines, not just the FPI lines.
